subproblem.title: Chart localization: N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)) and is compact, for a proper injective chart
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, N, W ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^d, ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P and v₀ ∈ V. Assume W is open, ψ is continuous on V and injective on V, ψ(V) = W ∩ N, and V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W. Then for every ε > 0 there is ρ > 0 such that B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ W, N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) ⊆ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)), and N ∩ B̄_ρ(ψ(v₀)) is compact.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (N W : Set (Euclid P)) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (v₀ : Euclid d), IsOpen W → ContinuousOn ψ V → InjOn ψ V → ψ '' V = W ∩ N → (∀ K ⊆ W, IsCompact K → IsCompact (V ∩ ψ ⁻¹' K)) → v₀ ∈ V → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ closedBall (ψ v₀) ρ ⊆ W ∧ N ∩ closedBall (ψ v₀) ρ ⊆ ψ '' (V ∩ ball v₀ ε) ∧ IsCompact (N ∩ closedBall (ψ v₀) ρ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 4(a) of the parent proof, written out directly with compact sets. Those steps say: ψ|_V : V → W ∩ N is a homeomorphism because ψ is proper into W, so ψ⁻¹ is continuous at y; and N ∩ B̄_{ρ₁} = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₁})) is compact. Put y := ψ(v₀); all balls in ℝ^P below are centred at y.
1. y ∈ W, because y = ψ(v₀) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N. As W is open, there is ρ₀ > 0 with B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W (take half the radius of an open ball about y contained in W).
2. K₀ := B̄_{ρ₀}(y) is compact (closed balls of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P are compact) and K₀ ⊆ W. So C₀ := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K₀) is compact by the properness hypothesis. Hence C := C₀ ∖ B_ε(v₀) is compact, being a compact set minus an open set.
3. C ⊆ V and ψ is continuous on V, so ψ(C) is compact, hence closed in ℝ^P.
4. y ∉ ψ(C). Indeed, suppose c ∈ C and ψ(c) = y = ψ(v₀). Then c = v₀, because c, v₀ ∈ V and ψ is injective on V. But v₀ ∈ B_ε(v₀) since ε > 0, whereas c ∉ B_ε(v₀).
5. By steps 3–4, the complement of ψ(C) is an open set containing y. So there is ρ₂ > 0 with B_{ρ₂}(y) ∩ ψ(C) = ∅. Put ρ := min(ρ₀, ρ₂/2) > 0. Then B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W and B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ B_{ρ₂}(y), so B̄_ρ(y) ∩ ψ(C) = ∅.
6. Inclusion. Let z ∈ N ∩ B̄_ρ(y). Then z ∈ W by step 5, so z ∈ W ∩ N = ψ(V): z = ψ(v) with v ∈ V. Since ψ(v) = z ∈ B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ K₀, we have v ∈ C₀. If v ∉ B_ε(v₀), then v ∈ C and z = ψ(v) ∈ ψ(C) ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ∅, which is impossible. Hence v ∈ V ∩ B_ε(v₀) and z ∈ ψ(V ∩ B_ε(v₀)).
7. Compactness. We claim N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y))). '⊆': as in step 6, z = ψ(v) with v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ρ(y). '⊇': if v ∈ V and ψ(v) ∈ B̄_ρ(y), then ψ(v) ∈ ψ(V) = W ∩ N ⊆ N. Since B̄_ρ(y) ⊆ W is compact, V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y)) is compact by properness. Its image under ψ, which is continuous on this subset of V, is compact.
8. Steps 5–7 give ρ > 0 with all three required properties. ∎
proof_key_steps: y = ψ(v₀) ∈ W; choose B̄_{ρ₀}(y) ⊆ W; by properness C := (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₀}(y))) ∖ B_ε(v₀) is compact.
ψ(C) is compact and misses y by injectivity of ψ on V, so some B̄_ρ(y) with ρ ≤ ρ₀ misses ψ(C).
Each z ∈ N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) is ψ(v) with v ∈ (V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_{ρ₀}(y))) ∖ C, so v ∈ B_ε(v₀).
N ∩ B̄_ρ(y) = ψ(V ∩ ψ⁻¹(B̄_ρ(y))) is compact by properness and continuity of ψ on V.

subproblem.title: Differentiated normality estimate ‖D(ψ∘g)(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2ab|x − ψ(g(x))|
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (O : Set (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → Euclid d) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P) (Q : Euclid d → (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen O → x ∈ O → DifferentiableAt ℝ g x → DifferentiableAt ℝ ψ (g x) → DifferentiableAt ℝ Q (g x) → (∀ z ∈ O, Q (g z) (z - ψ (g z)) = 0) → (Q (g x)).comp (fderiv ℝ ψ (g x)) = fderiv ℝ ψ (g x) → ‖Q (g x)‖ ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ a → 0 ≤ b → ‖fderiv ℝ Q (g x)‖ ≤ a → (∀ w : Euclid d, ‖w‖ ≤ b * ‖fderiv ℝ ψ (g x) w‖) → a * b * ‖x - ψ (g x)‖ ≤ 1 / 2 → ‖fderiv ℝ (ψ ∘ g) x‖ ≤ 1 + 2 * (a * b) * ‖x - ψ (g x)‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7(b)–(e) of the parent proof, with an abstract Q in place of P̂. The hypotheses are exactly the facts used there: ‖P̂(v)‖ ≤ 1, P̂(v) fixes range Dψ(v), ‖DP̂(v)‖ ≤ a, |w| ≤ b|Dψ(v)w|, and β|ν| ≤ 1/2 with β = ab. (The parent then applies |ν| ≤ |x − y|.) Write v := g(x), ν := x − ψ(v), A := Dg(x), B := Dψ(v) and π := ψ∘g. By the chain rule, Dπ(x) = B∘A.
1. Let F(z) := Q(g(z))(z − ψ(g(z))).
- z ↦ Q(g(z)) is differentiable at x with derivative h ↦ DQ(v)(Ah) (chain rule).
- z ↦ z − ψ(g(z)) is differentiable at x with derivative h ↦ h − BAh.
By the product rule for applying an operator-valued map to a vector-valued map (Mathlib HasFDerivAt.clm_apply), F is differentiable at x with DF(x)h = Q(v)(h − BAh) + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν.
2. F vanishes on the open neighbourhood O of x, so F has derivative 0 at x. By uniqueness of the Fréchet derivative, DF(x) = 0. Hence Q(v)h − Q(v)(BAh) + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν = 0 for every h ∈ ℝ^P.
3. By the hypothesis Q(v)∘B = B, Q(v)(BAh) = BAh = Dπ(x)h. Therefore Dπ(x)h = Q(v)h + (DQ(v)(Ah))ν.
4. Estimate. |Q(v)h| ≤ ‖Q(v)‖|h| ≤ |h|, and |(DQ(v)(Ah))ν| ≤ ‖DQ(v)(Ah)‖|ν| ≤ ‖DQ(v)‖|Ah||ν| ≤ a|Ah||ν|. The hypothesis with w := Ah gives |Ah| ≤ b|BAh| = b|Dπ(x)h|. Put s := ab|ν|; then 0 ≤ s ≤ 1/2, using a, b ≥ 0. So |Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + s|Dπ(x)h|.
5. Hence (1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h|. Since 0 ≤ s ≤ 1/2, (1 + 2s)(1 − s) = 1 + s(1 − 2s) ≥ 1. So |Dπ(x)h| ≤ (1 + 2s)(1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ (1 + 2s)|h|.
6. As h is arbitrary and 1 + 2s ≥ 0, ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2s = 1 + 2ab|ν| (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound). ∎
proof_key_steps: Differentiate F(z) = Q(g(z))(z − ψ(g(z))), which vanishes on O, at x: Q(v)(h − Dπ(x)h) + (DQ(v)(Dg(x)h))ν = 0.
Q(v) fixes Dπ(x)h = Dψ(v)Dg(x)h, so Dπ(x)h = Q(v)h + (DQ(v)(Dg(x)h))ν.
|Dg(x)h| ≤ b|Dπ(x)h| gives |Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| + ab|ν||Dπ(x)h|.
With s = ab|ν| ≤ 1/2, (1 − s)|Dπ(x)h| ≤ |h| and (1 + 2s)(1 − s) ≥ 1 give ‖Dπ(x)‖ ≤ 1 + 2s.

subproblem.title: The tangent projection v ↦ P̂(v) of a C² immersion is C¹
subproblem.statement: Let P, d ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^d open, and ψ : ℝ^d → ℝ^P C² on V with Dψ(v) injective for every v ∈ V. For v ∈ ℝ^d let P̂(v) ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) be the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto the subspace range Dψ(v), where Dψ(v) = fderiv ℝ ψ v (Lean: (fderiv ℝ ψ v).range.starProjection). Then v ↦ P̂(v) is C¹ on V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid d)) (ψ : Euclid d → Euclid P), IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 2 ψ V → (∀ z ∈ V, Injective (fderiv ℝ ψ z)) → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 (fun v => (fderiv ℝ ψ v).range.starProjection) V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2(a) of the parent proof: P̂(v) = D(v)G(v)⁻¹D(v)ᵀ with G = DᵀD is the orthogonal projection onto range D(v) and is C¹ on V. Notation: D(v) := Dψ(v) ∈ L(ℝ^d, ℝ^P). For A ∈ L(ℝ^d, ℝ^P), Aᵀ ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^d) is the adjoint, ⟨Aᵀh, w⟩ = ⟨h, Aw⟩ (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint, adjoint_inner_left).
1. D is C¹ on V. V is open and ψ is C² on V, so v ↦ D(v) is C¹ on V (Mathlib ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, with 1 + 1 ≤ 2).
2. A ↦ Aᵀ is a bounded ℝ-linear map L(ℝ^d, ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^d): it is additive, (cA)ᵀ = c̄Aᵀ = cAᵀ for real c, and ‖Aᵀ‖ = ‖A‖. A bounded linear map is C^∞ (Mathlib IsBoundedLinearMap.contDiff). So v ↦ D(v)ᵀ is C¹ on V.
3. G(v) := D(v)ᵀ ∘ D(v) ∈ L(ℝ^d, ℝ^d) is C¹ on V, since composition of operators is a bounded bilinear operation (Mathlib ContDiffOn.clm_comp).
4. G(v) is invertible for v ∈ V. For w ∈ ℝ^d, ⟨G(v)w, w⟩ = ⟨D(v)w, D(v)w⟩ = |D(v)w|². If G(v)w₁ = G(v)w₂, then G(v)(w₁ − w₂) = 0. Hence |D(v)(w₁ − w₂)|² = 0, so D(v)(w₁ − w₂) = 0, and w₁ = w₂ because D(v) is injective. An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^d is bijective (Mathlib LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo), with continuous inverse. So G(v) is a unit of the complete normed algebra L(ℝ^d, ℝ^d). (For d = 0 this algebra is the zero ring and all statements are trivial.)
5. Inversion is C^∞ at every unit of a complete normed algebra (Mathlib contDiffAt_ringInverse). G is C¹ and its values on V are units, so the composition v ↦ G(v)⁻¹ = Ring.inverse(G(v)) is C¹ on V.
6. R(v) := D(v) ∘ G(v)⁻¹ ∘ D(v)ᵀ is C¹ on V, again by ContDiffOn.clm_comp.
7. R(v) = P̂(v) for v ∈ V. Fix v ∈ V and h ∈ ℝ^P, and let u := R(v)h = D(v)(G(v)⁻¹D(v)ᵀh). Then u ∈ range D(v). Using G(v)G(v)⁻¹ = id, for every w ∈ ℝ^d:
⟨h − u, D(v)w⟩ = ⟨D(v)ᵀ(h − u), w⟩ = ⟨D(v)ᵀh − G(v)(G(v)⁻¹D(v)ᵀh), w⟩ = ⟨D(v)ᵀh − D(v)ᵀh, w⟩ = 0.
So h − u is orthogonal to range D(v). The orthogonal projection of h onto a subspace K is the unique u ∈ K with h − u ⊥ K (Mathlib Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero). Hence P̂(v)h = u = R(v)h for all h, i.e. R(v) = P̂(v).
8. P̂ agrees on V with the C¹ map R, so P̂ is C¹ on V (Mathlib ContDiffOn.congr). ∎
proof_key_steps: D = Dψ is C¹ on the open set V because ψ is C²; transposition is a bounded linear map, so v ↦ D(v)ᵀ is C¹.
G = DᵀD is C¹ on V and, since each D(v) is injective, invertible there; inversion is smooth at units, so G⁻¹ is C¹ on V.
R = DG⁻¹Dᵀ is C¹ on V, with R(v)h ∈ range D(v) and h − R(v)h ⊥ range D(v).
By the characterization of orthogonal projections R(v) = P̂(v) on V, so P̂ is C¹ on V.

- (v, e) ↦ ψ(v) is C¹ there, as ψ is C² on V;
- (v, e) ↦ e is continuous linear;
- (v, e) ↦ P̂(v)e is the application of the C¹ operator-valued map (v, e) ↦ P̂(v) to the continuous linear map (v, e) ↦ e (Mathlib ContDiffOn.clm_apply).
